overarching_objective: The student can discuss basic aspects of Chinese culture, including food, tea, family traditions, and famous landmarks, using simple A2 vocabulary and spoken phrases.
final_task: A role-play where the student acts as a cultural guide explaining Chinese traditions (food, tea, family, and landmarks) to the tutor, who plays a Saudi tourist planning a trip to China.

lessons.objective: The student can talk about famous Chinese landmarks and express a desire to visit them.
lessons.topic: The Great Wall and the capital city of Beijing.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The tutor asks the student what famous places they want to visit in China. The student verbally explains which places they want to see and why they are interesting.

lessons.objective: The student can offer a drink to a guest and describe traditional hospitality.
lessons.topic: How tea is served to guests in China, comparing it to Saudi coffee culture.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The student acts as a Chinese host offering tea to the tutor (the guest). The student verbally explains how to serve it and why it is polite.

lessons.objective: The student can describe simple meals and ingredients.
lessons.topic: Halal Chinese food (noodles, rice) and eating with chopsticks for a tourist.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The tutor plays a hungry tourist. The student verbally recommends a popular Chinese meal, describes what it is made with, and explains how to eat it with chopsticks.

lessons.objective: The student can talk about family traditions and showing respect to older people.
lessons.topic: Respecting elders and eating a traditional meal together as a family.
lessons.lesson_task: Guided discussion: The student verbally explains Chinese family traditions to the tutor, discussing how younger generations show respect to elders, and compares this to Saudi family life.

lessons.objective: The student can ask and answer questions about handmade objects.
lessons.topic: Chinese calligraphy and famous beautiful silk.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The student plays a shop owner selling famous traditional crafts. The tutor plays a customer asking questions about the silk and paint brushes. The student orally answers the questions.

lessons.objective: The student can explain the basic use of simple tools and inventions.
lessons.topic: How the compass and paper changed the world, becoming popular huge helps for travelers.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The student verbally explains a popular Chinese invention to the tutor, describing why it was invented and how it is a useful tool.

lessons.objective: The student can talk about past travel and buying/selling goods.
lessons.topic: Historical trade between China and the Middle East, exchanging silk and crafts.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The student acts as an ancient merchant on the Silk Road talking to the tutor (another merchant) about their long journey and what goods they want to trade.

lessons.objective: The student can compare two different places using simple adjectives.
lessons.topic: Comparing life in a busy modern city to a quiet village where generations live together.
lessons.lesson_task: Guided discussion: The tutor asks the student to compare a busy Chinese city to a quiet village. The student verbally uses comparisons to explain where they prefer to go on a journey.

lessons.objective: The student can discuss travel plans and what to pack.
lessons.topic: Preparing for a flight to see Chinese culture, acting as a tourist looking for delicious food.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The tutor and student verbally plan a trip to China. The student tells the tutor what to pack, which hotel to book, and what guidebook to buy.

lessons.objective: The student can give simple recommendations and explain basic cultural facts about China.
lessons.topic: A complete review of Chinese culture, covering food, tea, family, and landmarks.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The student acts as a cultural guide explaining Chinese traditions to the tutor, who plays a Saudi tourist planning a trip to China. The tutor should prompt the student to use vocabulary and phrases from L1-L9, asking follow-up questions such as 'What delicious food do you recommend? How do families show respect? What famous traditional places should I see?'
